spec.title: PP-003 — Option C: the advisor slice (V4)
spec.p: _Filed: 2026-07-11 · Status: **POSTPONED** (owner cut it from Campaign 3 Stage B — «отдельная задача, запланируй») · Origin: RP-C3-1 ruling (Stage B plan §1, §8); scope options §3; decision D-C3-7._

section.title: The task
section.p: Build the **advisor channel** (VISION §V4) — the fabric's fourth plane, on top of Stage B's descent + ascent. An advisor is a worker-shaped run that returns *advice*, not owned work: a weaker caller asks a stronger profile a bounded question and keeps ownership of its task.

list.item: an `advice` packet type — worker-shaped run, **no ownership transfer** (the caller stays responsible for the task);

a capability bar on the CALLER: `advisor_enabled ⇐ caller_class ≥ medium` — routing by capability, not by task difficulty (RD-10: weak callers are made WORSE by advice; the SWE-1.5→1.6 threshold, the minRLM-nano inversion);
context hand-off ≈ a fork of the caller's context (RD-11's clean-context posture applies);
an accounting line: the advice call bills the **caller's** budget (revisit trigger: first field data — RD-10).

section.title: Why postponed
section.p: The owner ruled RP-C3-1 as **Option B** (descent + ascent) and cut Option C explicitly: «Вариант C с адвайзором - отдельная задача, запланируй.» V4 is a real plane with its own economics (inverted vs descent), its own capability bar, and its own trial questions — folding it into Stage B would widen the campaign past the descent core the owner wants first. D-C3-7 stays drafted in the Stage B plan but out of its build scope.

section.title: Unblock
section.p: The owner commissions **Stage C** (or folds the advisor into a later mandate). Design questions to settle at commissioning:

list.item: the caller-class threshold's exact boundary and how a caller measures its own class at call time;
which uncertainty signal(s) fire the trigger, and their thresholds (measured, not guessed);
whose budget line pays when advice recurses (caller's, per the draft — confirm against first field data);
the trial that proves advice HELPS a medium caller and does not hurt a weak one (the RD-10 inversion is the falsifier).
Re-read D-C3-7, RD-10, RD-11 (RLM-SYNTHESIS §3), FD-6/FD-8 (FUGU-SYNTHESIS §3), VISION §V4 — the advisor-ladder pillar.

Confirm Stage B shipped the plumbing D-C3-7 reuses (worker-run shape, `context_from` access lists, the acceptance/clean-context posture) — the advisor is "a worker run with an `advice` packet type", so most of the seam already exists after Stage B.
Draft the Stage C plan (or slice) with its own MT pre-registration for the help/hurt trial.
Decision + scope: Stage B plan §3 (Option C), §4 (D-C3-7), §1 (RP-C3-1 ruling) — [`FRACTALITY-RLM-PLAN-v0.1.xml`](../../fractality/v0.1.0/spec/plans/FRACTALITY-RLM-PLAN-v0.1.xml)
